headline: OpenAI will start notifying parents if their teen has been kicked off ChatGPT for violence
summary: The new feature alerts guardians if a child's account is deactivated due to policy violations related to violent threats or acts, expanding existing parental controls.
details: OpenAI has expanded its parental controls for ChatGPT, now notifying parents with linked accounts if their teenage child's account is deactivated. This occurs specifically for violations of policies related to violent threats or acts of violence online.

The system sends an initial alert about an 'important update' regarding the child's account. Parents can then click 'Learn More' to access a detailed message explaining the deactivation due to 'Acts of Violence' policy breaches.

This feature was developed in collaboration with Moonshot, a firm specializing in countering online violence. Moonshot's founder, Vidhya Ramalingam, emphasized that these notifications are a critical first step for families to intervene and seek help early.

The move follows scrutiny after a 2025 Tumbler Ridge mass shooting suspect reportedly used ChatGPT, and OpenAI faced criticism for not notifying authorities when the shooter's account was banned. OpenAI chief Sam Altman had apologized for the oversight.

In addition to these new notifications, OpenAI has also introduced a 'Study Mode' that can be enabled from parental controls, offering hints before answers to aid learning. The platform will also provide more frequent break reminders for teens spending extended time on ChatGPT.

headline: LG monitors silently install McAfee via Windows Update without user consent
summary: LG monitors are reportedly installing software that promotes McAfee subscriptions through Windows Update, all without explicit user approval. This behavior has been reproduced and affects various models.
details: Connecting some LG monitors to a Windows PC may automatically install software promoting McAfee subscriptions. Gamers Nexus successfully reproduced this behavior with an LG UltraGear 34GX900A-B after user reports.

The installation, identified as 'LG Monitor App Installer', occurs silently via Windows Update, following LG extension and software component packages. Users receive no consent prompt or approval request.
Gamers Nexus observed the McAfee promotion in 31 out of 32 consecutive system boots. The popup offers a 30-day trial that automatically converts into a paid subscription.
This issue is not limited to new displays; an LG UltraFine 32UN880-B purchased three years prior also exhibited the behavior. User complaints about the installer date back to at least 2024.
The LG Monitor App Installer is listed with broad capabilities, including access to the internet and all system resources. Gamers Nexus also highlighted concerns regarding LG’s privacy documents.
Such automatic software delivery isn't exclusive to LG. Dell also uses Windows Update to install Alienware Command Center for compatible peripherals, as confirmed by Gamers Nexus's own testing.
Users can prevent these automatic downloads by enabling 'Prevent automatic download of applications associated with device metadata' in Windows Group Policy settings.
However, blocking this setting may also prevent useful monitor or peripheral software from installing automatically, requiring users to download such applications manually.
